title: Tangential velocity BCs not obeyed during mesh deformation
body: The mesh deformation plugins in ASPECT are designed to deform the mesh without deforming the material. When the mesh is deformed, so too is the boundary of the domain. It should be possible to apply tangential velocity boundary conditions to deforming boundaries. The current codebase incorrectly constrains tangential velocity boundary conditions because it always uses the boundary normal from the start of the first time step (which is before even initial mesh deformations have taken place). As a result, tangential velocity BCs can inadvertently result in inflow/outflow. For example, [this test](https://github.com/bobmyhill/aspect/blob/tangential_velocity_mesh_deformation/tests/function_mesh_deformation_tangential_mesh_velocity_simple_shear.prm) exhibits horizontal velocities at the top of the domain even after it has been tilted: @gassmoeller and I had a first try at fixing the problem here: https://github.com/bobmyhill/aspect/tree/tangential_velocity_mesh_deformation specifically, shifting a call to `VectorTools::compute_no_normal_flux_constraints` from [Simulator::compute_initial_velocity_boundary_constraints](https://github.com/bobmyhill/aspect/blob/b3f8b314d0685c9d7ad2d8bd7be4e3c1c8bd0f18/source/simulator/core.cc#L1376) to [Simulator::compute_current_velocity_boundary_constraints](https://github.com/bobmyhill/aspect/blob/b3f8b314d0685c9d7ad2d8bd7be4e3c1c8bd0f18/source/simulator/core.cc#L1403) Although this modification seems to correct the tangential velocities in the 0th timestep (for example, in a [test](https://github.com/bobmyhill/aspect/blob/tangential_velocity_mesh_deformation/tests/hill_diffusion_simple_shear.prm) involving a non-zero initial mesh deformation and subsequent hill diffusion), it results in very strange behaviour for [this test](https://github.com/bobmyhill/aspect/blob/tangential_velocity_mesh_deformation/tests/function_mesh_deformation_tangential_mesh_velocity_simple_shear.prm): @tjhei, @anne-glerum, any ideas?
